text: Widespread adoption suggests many individuals, including parents seeking sensitive pediatric guidance, increasingly depending on public AI platforms. However, these “black box” systems risk generating inaccurate or inconsistent advice. Thus, evaluating AI’s pediatric diagnostic accuracy is clinically significant, as empirical evidence for differentiating ASD remains scarce. To address this gap, this study systematically evaluates the performance of AI platforms in identifying ASD from standardized pediatric case studies and distinguishing it from other neurodevelopmental conditions across three dimensions: diagnostic accuracy, concordance with clinical benchmarks, and ASD classification. By comparing multipurpose and medically oriented systems, this study highlights AI’s potential as a supportive tool for complex pediatric synthesis while investigating the risks of public reliance on potentially misleading automated information.
source_label: An in-silico comparative cross-sectional diagnostic- accuracy study evaluating artificial intelligence platforms in identifying autism spectrum disorder from standardized pediatric case vignettes 2026
